{{Quote|The last known location of the ''Krieger'' was in the Hanod system.|Airen Cracken, ''Wanted by Cracken''|<ref name="Wanted">[[Wanted by Cracken (sourcebook)|''Wanted by Cracken'']]</ref>}}
The '''Hanod system''' was a part of the [[Corva sector/Legends|Corva sector]]<ref name="EAOC" /> in the [[New Territories/Legends|New Territories]] portion of<ref name="TEA" /> the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]].<ref name="EAOC" /> It contained the terrestrial astronomical object [[Hanod]].<ref name="Written" /> In [[7 ABY/Legends|7 ABY]],<ref name="Date">[[Wanted by Cracken (sourcebook)|''Wanted by Cracken'']] is dated to three [[Standard year/Legends|years]] after the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|Battle of Endor]]. Since ''[[The New Essential Chronology]]'' dates that conflict to [[4 ABY/Legends|4 ABY]], the placement of the sourcebook therefore translates to [[7 ABY/Legends|7 ABY]].</ref> [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]] [[General/Legends|General]] [[Airen Cracken/Legends|Airen Cracken]] listed the Hanod [[Star system/Legends|system]] as the last known location of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Imperial]] [[Star Destroyer/Legends|Star Destroyer]] ''[[Krieger]]'' in an entry of the [[Datafile/Legends|datafile]] ''[[Wanted by Cracken]]'' dedicated to Imperial [[Captain/Legends|Captain]] [[Dor Reder]].<ref name="Wanted" />

==Behind the scenes==
The Hanod system was first mentioned in the [[1993]] ''[[Star Wars: The Roleplaying Game]]'' supplement [[Wanted by Cracken (sourcebook)|''Wanted by Cracken'']], which was written by [[Louis J. Prosperi]] for [[West End Games]].<ref name="Wanted" /> The [[2009]] reference book ''[[The Essential Atlas]]'' placed the system in grid square P-3.<ref name="TEA" /> Although the entry for the Hanod system in the [[2008]] ''[[The Complete Star Wars Encyclopedia]]'' claims that it was situated in the [[Trans-Hydian/Legends|Borderland Regions]],<ref name="CSWE">{{CSWECite|II|14|Hanod system}}</ref> that placement was overridden by ''The Essential Atlas'', which established that the region did not, in fact, intersect square P-3.<ref name="TEA" />
